title: Hydroxychloroquine and chloroquine retinopathy: recommendations on monitoring
text: The Royal College of Ophthalmologists recommends retinopathy monitoring for adults taking hydroxychloroquine or chloroquine. People taking hydroxychloroquine without added risk factors start annual monitoring after five years of therapy; with added risk factors, annual monitoring can start after one year. Chloroquine is more retinotoxic, so annual monitoring starts after one year. Risk factors that justify earlier monitoring are a hydroxychloroquine dose above 5 mg/kg/day by body weight, concomitant tamoxifen, renal impairment with eGFR below 60 ml/min/1.73m2, and chloroquine use, for which the suggested safe dose is below 2.3 mg/kg/day. Monitoring uses spectral domain OCT and widefield fundus autofluorescence for everyone. Automated visual fields with a white stimulus are added only if imaging is abnormal, using a 10 2 pattern for parafoveal changes and a 30 2 pattern for pericentral changes; multifocal electroretinography is used if structural abnormalities persist without a matching field defect. Baseline examination is no longer recommended for new starters, because baseline findings rarely led to stopping the drug and the testing used substantial resources. Monitoring is annual, not more often, and stops if the drug is stopped.
